# Sirach Chapter 6 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 6 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_006_page_001.jpg

---

6:1 Do not become an enemy instead of a friend, for a bad name brings shame and reproach — so it is with the double-tongued sinner.

6:2 Do not exalt yourself by your own soul's counsel, lest your soul be torn apart like a bull.

6:3 Your leaves will be devoured and your fruit will be destroyed, and you will be left like a dry tree.

6:4 An evil soul destroys the one who has it, and makes it the laughingstock of its enemies.

6:5 A pleasant word multiplies friends, and a gracious tongue multiplies greetings.

6:6 Let those who are at peace with you be many, but let your advisors be one in a thousand.

6:7 When you gain a friend, gain him first by testing; do not be quick to trust him.

6:8 For there is a friend who is such only for a season, and he will not abide in the day of your trouble.

6:9 And there is a friend who turns into an enemy, and he will disclose a quarrel to your shame.

6:10 And there is a friend who is a table-companion, but he will not stand firm in the day of your affliction.

6:11 When things go well with you, he is like another self, and he freely commands your servants.

6:12 But if you are brought low, he will be against you and will hide from your face.

6:13 Separate yourself from your enemies, and be on guard with your friends.

6:14 A faithful friend is a sturdy shelter; whoever finds one has found a treasure.

6:15 A faithful friend is beyond price, and no scales can weigh his worth.

6:16 A faithful friend is a life-saving medicine; those who fear the Lord will find one.

6:17 Whoever fears the Lord makes true friendships, for as he is, so also is his neighbor.

6:18 My child, from your youth up receive instruction, and until you are old you will keep finding wisdom.

6:19 Come to her like one who plows and sows, and wait for her good harvest; for in cultivating her you will toil only a little while, and soon you will eat of her produce.

6:20 How very harsh she is to the undisciplined! The senseless person cannot abide in her.

6:21 She will lie on him like a heavy stone of testing, and he will not be slow to cast her aside.

6:22 For discipline is like her name; she is not apparent to many.

6:23 Listen, my child, and accept my judgment; do not reject my counsel.

6:24 Put your feet into her fetters, and your neck into her collar.

6:25 Put your shoulder under her and carry her, and do not be weary of her bonds.

6:26 Come to her with all your soul, and keep her ways with all your might.

6:27 Search her out, inquire and seek, and she will be made known to you; and when you get hold of her, do not let go.

6:28 For at last you will find the rest she gives, and she will be transformed into your joy.

6:29 Her fetters will become for you a strong defense, and her collar a glorious robe.

6:30 There is golden ornament upon her, and her bonds are a blue thread.

6:31 You will wear her like a glorious robe, and put her on like a crown of gladness.

6:32 If you are willing, my child, you will be taught; and if you apply yourself, you will become clever.

6:33 If you love to listen, you will gain knowledge; and if you pay attention, you will become wise.

6:34 Stand in the assembly of the elders; whoever is wise, cling to him.

6:35 Be glad to hear every account of godliness, and let no proverb of understanding escape you.

6:36 When you see a man of understanding, rise early to visit him; let your foot wear out his doorstep.

6:37 Reflect on the statutes of the Lord, and meditate on his commandments always; it is he who will give insight to your mind, and your desire for wisdom will be granted.

---

*Translator's Note: The chapter falls into two main sections: (1) the three kinds of friends (vv.1-17) and (2) the pursuit of Wisdom framed as agricultural labor and then as disciplined apprenticeship (vv.18-37). "Fetters" and "collar" in vv.24-30 are deliberate paradoxes — what appears like bondage is revealed as glory. Hebrew (Cairo Genizah MS A) is extant for parts of this chapter.*
